F1.quote: Mapping Manuscript Migrations uses semantic technologies to unite records from three datasets: the Schoenberg Database of Manuscripts at the University of Pennsylvania, the Bibale database at the Institut de recherche et d’histoire des textes, and the Medieval Manuscripts Catalogue at the University of Oxford.
F1.claim: the project defined by its documentation site: semantic technologies uniting records from three named datasets at three institutions
F1.lineage: what it is: three manuscript databases united as one linked-data knowledge graph of manuscript history and provenance

F2.quote: This project is a partnership between four institutions, funded under Round 4 of the Trans-Atlantic Platform’s Digging into Data Challenge.
F2.claim: a partnership of four institutions, funded under Round 4 of the Digging into Data Challenge

F3.quote: Contributors include the Schoenberg Institute for Manuscript Studies at the University of Pennsylvania, the Bodleian Library and the Oxford e-Research Centre at the University of Oxford, the Institut de recherche et d’histoire des textes, and the Semantic Computing Research Group at Aalto University, Helsinki.
F3.claim: the contributing units: SIMS (Penn), the Bodleian and the Oxford e-Research Centre, IRHT, Aalto's Semantic Computing Research Group

F4.quote: This website hosts the technical documentation for the Mapping Manuscript Migrations (MMM) project, including the MMM Data Model , Schema , and Data Transformation Pipeline .
F4.claim: the site is the project's technical documentation: data model, schema, transformation pipeline
F4.lineage: the carrier: RDF mapped to a unified model from CIDOC-CRM and FRBR

F5.quote: The MMM project mapped and transformed three separate datasets against the unified MMM data model: the The Schoenberg Database of Manuscripts , Bibale , and the Medieval Manuscripts in Oxford Libraries catalogue. Each dataset’s original structure and format impacted the development and implementation of the MMM data model.
F5.claim: the three datasets mapped against one data model, whose development each dataset's own structure shaped
F5.lineage: the carrier: RDF mapped to a unified model from CIDOC-CRM and FRBR

F6.quote: Use the public portal to search and browse the unified MMM data, or visit our blog to learn more about the project. … You can also download the entire MMM dataset from Zenodo: https://zenodo.org/record/4019643
F6.claim: access by the public portal and by download of the whole dataset from Zenodo (record 4019643)
F6.lineage: access: LDF.fi SPARQL endpoint, the semantic portal, the Zenodo copy

F7.quote: The Mapping Manuscript Migrations (MMM) project transformed three separate datasets relating to the history and provenance of medieval and Renaissance manuscripts into a unified knowledge graph.
F7.claim: the data paper's definition: three datasets on manuscript history and provenance transformed into one knowledge graph
F7.lineage: what it is: three manuscript databases united as one linked-data knowledge graph of manuscript history and provenance

F8.quote: The source databases are: Schoenberg Database of Manuscripts, from the Schoenberg Institute for Manuscript Studies, University of Pennsylvania; Bibale, from the Institut de recherche et d’histoire des textes (IRHT-CNRS, Paris); and Medieval Manuscripts in Oxford Libraries, from the Bodleian Libraries, University of Oxford.
F8.claim: the three source databases by their holders
F8.lineage: its sources: the Schoenberg Database, Bibale and the Oxford catalogue

F9.quote: The data consist of more than 20 million RDF triples which have been mapped to the MMM Data Model. The model combines classes and properties from CIDOC-CRM and FRBR, together with some specific MMM elements.
F9.claim: more than 20 million RDF triples, mapped to a model combining CIDOC-CRM and FRBR with MMM elements
F9.lineage: the carrier: RDF mapped to a unified model from CIDOC-CRM and FRBR

F10.quote: The MMM dataset is available from the Zenodo repository, and can be directly deployed on a SPARQL endpoint using a docker recipe. To test and demonstrate its usefulness, the MMM Knowledge Graph is in use in the MMM Semantic Portal
F10.claim: the dataset on Zenodo, deployable by docker recipe; the portal as its test and demonstration
F10.lineage: access: LDF.fi SPARQL endpoint, the semantic portal, the Zenodo copy

F11.quote: The Mapping Manuscript Migrations project (MMM) links disparate datasets from Europe and North America to provide an international view of the history and provenance of medieval and Renaissance manuscripts
F11.claim: it links European and North American datasets for an international view of manuscript history and provenance
F11.lineage: an international view: datasets from Europe and North America

F12.quote: The aggregated data can be browsed and visualized at scales ranging from an individual manuscript to more than 2167,000 manuscripts in total.

The second component is the MMM semantic portal, which is designed to test and demonstrate the platform for use by researchers
F13.claim: two components: the Linked Open Data service on LDF.fi and the semantic portal
F13.lineage: access: LDF.fi SPARQL endpoint, the semantic portal, the Zenodo copy

F14.quote: a relational database containing more than 240,000 records for manuscript observations); … a relational database containing nearly 13,000 manuscript records); … a collection of more than 10,000 XML documents).
F14.claim: the sources' sizes: SDBM 240,000+ observation records, Bibale nearly 13,000 manuscript records, Oxford 10,000+ XML documents
F14.lineage: its sources: the Schoenberg Database, Bibale and the Oxford catalogue

F15.quote: Instances of the four main classes of entities (Manuscripts, Works, Actors, and Places) have been reconciled in two ways: automatically through the use of Linked Open Data authorities like VIAF (Virtual International Authority File) and TGN (Thesaurus of Geographic Names) where possible, as well as by manual comparison of specific entities identified by string similarity
F15.claim: manuscripts, works, actors and places reconciled automatically through VIAF and TGN, and manually by string similarity
F15.lineage: the unit: the manuscript, reconciled across sources

F16.quote: The original data have not been corrected or amended in any way by the MMM project. The source information for each resource in the unified data has been retained by MMM, so that users can always refer back to the original dataset and can limit their use of the MMM data by source if required. Errors and omissions in the data should be reported to the owners of the source datasets.
F16.claim: the data are uncorrected; each resource keeps its source information, so users can refer back and filter by source; errors go to the source owners
F16.lineage: its stated limits: an aggregator, not a data manager; sources uncorrected; unstructured provenance

F41.quote: The transparent relationship between the source datasets and the MMM data underscores the role of MMM as an aggregator of data rather than as a data management system, though an unanticipated but welcome outcome of the project has been its ability to help managers of the original datasets to identify problems. Because data correction is not part of the MMM transformation process, weaknesses, inconsistencies, and errors in the datasets become clear in search results, alerting dataset managers that something needs to be fixed at their end.
